questions.q: Why do external portal users need a different sharing model than Doverfield's internal employees?
options: External users aren't employees and don't belong in the role hierarchy at all; their access is scoped by the Account they're associated with via a Contact instead
External users automatically inherit the access of whichever employee created their login
External users cannot be granted access to any Salesforce object under any circumstances
External users always see every record in the org by default
questions.explain: Role hierarchy assumes an internal management structure that external users simply aren't part of -- Experience Cloud scopes their access through the Account relationship instead.

questions.q: What organization-wide default setting does this sharing pattern require as its baseline?
options: Public Read/Write, so sharing sets have something to restrict
Private, so a portal user starts out seeing nothing until a defined mechanism explicitly grants access
Public Read Only, since portal users should never edit records
There is no OWD requirement for this pattern
questions.explain: The pattern only works safely if the object starts at Private -- everything a portal user is allowed to see then has to come from an explicit, defined grant like a sharing set, never from a looser default.

questions.q: What does a sharing set specifically do in Doverfield's portal design?
options: It manually grants access to one customer account at a time, requiring reconfiguration for every new customer
It defines an account-based access mapping, configured once, that automatically shares the matching object's records with any external user whose Account matches the record's Account
It removes the need for an organization-wide default entirely
It converts external users into internal role-hierarchy users
questions.explain: A sharing set is configured once and applies automatically to every user it covers, as new customer accounts are added, which is exactly why it scales without per-account setup.

questions.q: Why does a plain Customer Community license rely on sharing sets rather than role-based sharing?
options: Because a plain Customer Community license has no role hierarchy at all, so sharing sets are the tool built specifically for that license tier
Because role-based sharing is deprecated in all Salesforce orgs
Because sharing sets are a legacy feature being phased out in favor of role-based sharing
Because Customer Community users are not allowed to see any Case or Order records
questions.explain: Sharing sets exist precisely because the base Customer Community license tier doesn't support role hierarchy -- they're the purpose-built mechanism for that tier, not a workaround for a missing feature.

questions.q: In the lab scenario, why can't a plain sharing set alone satisfy the enterprise customer's request for three different internal visibility levels among their own purchasing staff?
options: Sharing sets grant access based on matching the user's Account to the record's Account, not on finer-grained distinctions like who personally opened a specific Case within the same account
Sharing sets cannot be used for Case objects at all
Sharing sets only work for internal employees, never external users
The requirement is impossible to satisfy with any Salesforce licensing tier
questions.explain: A sharing set's access mapping works at the Account-match level -- it doesn't natively distinguish between different people within the same external account the way a higher, role-based license tier would.
